subject: Velox integration: technical validation & solution review
messages:
From: Amit Patel <amit.patel@velox.consulting>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tara Lee <tara.lee@velox.consulting>, infra@cloudforge.com
Date: 2026-08-25T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Velox <> Redwood: request for technical validation and joint reference design review

Hi Hannah,

Thanks for the quick intro via LinkedIn — I’m Amit, technical lead at Velox Consulting. We’ve been piloting a managed orchestration layer that routes inference calls to multiple providers, and we’re planning a deeper integration with Redwood’s API for routing, caching, and cost-aware fallbacks. Before we commit to a joint customer proof-of-concept, Velox would like a solution architecture review and a short technical validation (smoke test) plan to check compatibility with our runtime.

High-level asks:
- Short (60-90 minute) architecture review call to walk through the reference design.
- Validation of streaming + function-calling semantics, KV cache behavior, and recovery/fallback policies.
- A basic performance target: 95th pct latency under our typical P95 payload (avg sequence length ~400 tokens, median concurrency 30).
- A draft test harness we can run in our sandbox with Redwood test account credentials.

We’ve attached an initial reference diagram and CloudForge infra diagram. Can you share who on Redwood should join (solutions architecture, partner engineering, and a runtime engineer)? We’d prefer next-week times Tues/Wed afternoon PT.

Attachments: velox_integration_reference_arch_v1.pdf, cloudforge_infra_diagram.png

Thanks,
Amit Patel
Technical Lead, Velox Consulting
amit.patel@velox.consulting
+1 415-555-0167

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Amit Patel <amit.patel@velox.consulting>
Cc: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Tara Lee <tara.lee@velox.consulting>
Date: 2026-08-29T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Velox <> Redwood: request for technical validation and joint reference design review

Hi all — quick technical notes ahead of the call so we can be efficient on Wed:

1) Streaming & function-calls- We’ll validate both streaming text-only and streaming with tool/function frames. Important: Velox must preserve the same token boundaries when doing partial-prefetch fallbacks — otherwise function args can be malformed. We’ll run a simple round-trip test that splits a prompt mid-token to make sure fallbacks don't lose state.

2) KV cache consistency- Need clarity on expected TTL and whether Velox's routing will ever hit multiple regions mid-conversation. If so, we recommend a short TTL + sticky routing per conversation id for 48 hours. We can test KV staleness by toggling model variants in-flight and verifying "+cache_miss" traces in our logs.

3) Performance targets and load profile- The 400-token average and concurrency 30 is reasonable. For an apples-to-apples test we’ll run three profiles: low (10 concurrent), target (30 concurrent), and stress (100 concurrent) and measure token/sec, P50/P95, and tail latency. Mateo, can you prepare a lightweight harness that uses our sandbox endpoint and produces the token-level traces? I’ll own the analysis and dashboards.

4) Test data and credentials- Amit: please upload a representative set of 20 prompts (sanitized) to the shared drive and create a Velox dev key with read-only routing scope for redwood-integ-test. We’ll need it by EOD Mon 2026-08-31 to run a warm-up smoke test.

I’ve attached a short checklist of traces we’ll collect and the agreed-on success criteria.

Cheers,
Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.ai
